questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you, should you pull to the right side of the road and let it pass?
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, you must pull to the right side of the road immediately and let it pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates, Disabled Veteran license plates, or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement can cause you to lose control of your car. Slow down when you see wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching the end of a divided highway.
You are approaching the beginning of a divided highway.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching the beginning of a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway begins ahead. Keep to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: During a tire blowout, should you brake quickly and pull off the roadway to check the tire?
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly during a blowout. Instead, ease off the gas pedal, grip the steering wheel firmly, and pull safely off the road. Then check your tires.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Eating, drinking coffee, or showering cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: If a driver refuses to submit to testing, will their driving privileges be suspended for only three months?
questions.explanation: If you refuse to submit to chemical testing, your driving privileges will be suspended for one year. If you are under 21, the suspension is six months.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about motorist services. These include rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

questions.question: A teen driver can have only two passengers under age 20 in the vehicle during the first 12 months of licensing.
questions.explanation: During the first 12 months, a teen driver (ages 16-17) can have only one passenger under age 20. Exception: siblings, steplings, children, or stepchildren are allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: You may not pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop before reaching it. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On divided highways with a median, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: White rectangular signs show rules you must obey. This sign means do not pass other vehicles for any reason.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
questions.explanation: At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: It is safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads. Your tires may lose grip and you will lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must bear either right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns that the road splits and you must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: When daylight starts to fade, what lights should you use so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades. Use high beam headlights only when driving in an open area with no other vehicles around.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic lights are ahead at an intersection. Warning signs are yellow with black markings.

questions.question: After stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, can you turn left on a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street with traffic moving left?
questions.explanation: You can turn left at a red light when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street with traffic moving left. You must stop completely first and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: On a two-lane road, must you always stop for a stopped school bus?
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Do not stop in an intersection if possible. You can drive again after the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagon-shaped sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road. You can only pass on the right if you can do so without leaving the roadway.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a problem.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed and let crossing or merging vehicles go first. Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a conflict.

questions.question: How do alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?

options.text: They affect both alertness and coordination.

questions.correctAnswerText: They affect both alertness and coordination.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If the fog is too thick to see through, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.
